property_summary: After any call to setOwner, owner should equal the argument _owner, but the buggy version leaves owner unchanged.
For any caller, if the caller is not the original deployer (admin), the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy version allows a non-admin to change the owner.
After the contract deployment, only the admin can successfully change the owner; the bug allows any caller, including a non-admin, to change the owner.
For any non-admin caller, setOwner should not change the owner; the buggy version changes owner to the caller when the caller is not the admin, violating access control.

For a non-admin caller, setOwner must never alter the owner; the buggy version incorrectly sets owner to that caller if they are the admin, satisfying the admin requirement but still changing owner to msg.sender.
For any caller, after a setOwner call that succeeds, the owner must equal the _owner argument; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead, breaking this invariant.

For any address 'newOwner' and any caller, after a call to setOwner(newOwner) that does not revert, the owner must equal newOwner; the buggy version sets owner to msg.sender instead, so it always fails this equality when sender is not the admin (reverts) or when sender is the admin but the parameter differs from sender.

The onlyAdmin modifier always restricts setOwner to the original admin for any caller; the bug allows the current owner to bypass the admin check, letting the owner change 'owner' while the admin cannot once the owner differs.
The owner can be changed only by the original admin; the bug allows the current owner to change the owner even when that caller is not the original admin.

After any call to setOwner, the stored owner must equal the caller if the caller is the original admin; the bug allows a non-admin owner to change owner and thus break the invariant that only the original admin can change owner.
For any caller that is not the original admin (_deployer), a call to setOwner must revert; the bug allows a non-admin current owner to successfully change the owner.

For any caller, if the caller is not the original admin (msg.sender of the constructor), a call to setOwner must revert; the bug allows the current owner (who may not be the original admin) to call setOwner successfully.
